title: WIM puts talent, workplaces and women-led enterprise at heart of global competitiveness | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 18 September 2026 00:05
-     - 45

Women in Management Global Founder Dr. Sulochana Segera

Women MSME Awards 2026 Chairman Prashantha Mahadevan

NextTier Mentorship and Leadership Awards 2026 Dr. Rohantha Athukorala

UK Qualification Network Director 

Tim Dawkins

By Amira Cader

“Sri Lanka must move beyond academic qualifications and domestic recognition to build the skills, leadership, innovation and international exposure needed to compete in the global economy,” Women in Management Global (WIM) Founder and Chairperson Dr. Sulochana Segera said.

She made the observation at the launch of WIM – The Business & Leadership Night 2026, which will bring together three flagship platforms focusing on women-led enterprise, next-generation leadership and responsible workplaces on 9 December.

The landmark event will unite the second Women MSME Awards 2026, the Respectful Workplace Audit & Certification and the second NextTier Mentorship & Awards 2026, as WIM seeks to connect business recognition with leadership development and internationally aligned workplace practices.

Segera said Sri Lanka needed to rethink how it develops and positions its human capital, arguing that academic qualifications alone were no longer sufficient in a rapidly changing business environment.

“A degree is important, but a degree alone cannot determine success in today’s global economy, stressing that skills, discipline, innovation, leadership, technological adaptability, international exposure and the ability to execute were becoming increasingly important.

She said Sri Lanka must also examine whether its relatively educated population was being effectively translated into greater economic productivity and global competitiveness.

“It is time for Sri Lanka to move beyond simply participating in the global economy and start competing,” Segera stressed.

She also highlighted the need to strengthen Sri Lanka’s international visibility, noting that the country often spoke about its talent and capabilities domestically without doing enough to showcase them overseas. WIM’s expansion into seven countries, she said, had partly been driven by the objective of promoting Sri Lankan women and their professional, entrepreneurial and leadership capabilities internationally.

Segera said the Business and Leadership Night was an extension of this ambition, bringing entrepreneurship, leadership development and responsible workplace practices together while providing greater visibility for Sri Lankan talent and corporate excellence.

She also called for greater economic participation by women, particularly given their strong representation within higher education, arguing that Sri Lanka could not afford to leave a significant segment of its talent outside productive economic activity.

“If we don’t get them into economic participation, we can’t move forward,” she said.

However, Segera stressed that advancing women should not be treated solely as a women’s issue and called for greater involvement from men, businesses and other stakeholders.

“Leadership has no gender. It’s the way we approach it,” she noted.

NextTier Mentorship & Awards Chairman Dr. Rohantha Athukorala said rapid technological and economic changes were fundamentally altering traditional employment and career pathways, increasing the importance of mentorship and continuous skills development.

“The job arena has changed drastically,” he said.

Athukorala pointed particularly to artificial intelligence, which he said was already transforming how businesses operate, market themselves and access information.

He said the changing environment meant both young people entering employment and established professionals needed to continuously reassess their capabilities and understand where new opportunities were emerging.

NextTier seeks to address this gap by exposing participants to areas including AI, analytics, FinTech, project management, recruitment, leadership, management and macroeconomics.

“I think it is a fantastic innovation adding that helping even a relatively small number of people identify the right career direction and emerging industries could generate wider value for Sri Lanka” Athukorala said.

For the second consecutive year, the program will select 35 participants for structured engagement with 12 local and international WIM Global mentors, providing access to their experience and perspectives in preparation for greater leadership responsibilities.

Women MSME Awards 2026 judging panel Chair Prashantha Mahadevan said the awards would recognise entrepreneurs not only for business success, but also for the wider economic and social impact they create.

“The Women MSME Awards 2026 are not simply about recognising businesses that are successful. They are about recognising women who are going beyond running a business,” he said.

“We are looking at women who are creating employment, generating economic value, driving innovation and making a positive social impact.”

Mahadevan said the judging process would take into account the individual journeys of entrepreneurs, recognising that businesses develop under different circumstances and with varying levels of resources.

“Every business has a story, and every entrepreneur has faced different challenges,” he said.

Employment creation would be an important consideration in the evaluation process, he added.

“When a woman entrepreneur creates jobs, she is not only growing her own business. She is creating opportunities for other people and supporting families and communities.”

Innovation would also be considered broadly, ranging from products and services to technology adoption and new approaches to solving business and social challenges.

The Women MSME Awards will recognise entrepreneurs across 10 categories. Nominations will be open from September 20 to October 20 2026 via www.womeninmanagementawards.org.

Alongside entrepreneurship and leadership development, WIM is introducing the Respectful Workplace Audit and Certification to encourage organisations to benchmark their workplace practices against internationally aligned standards.

The initiative will assess organisations against International Finance Corporation (IFC) Respectful Workplace guidelines, with qualifying organisations receiving WIM endorsement and certification in partnership with TLM UK, an Ofqual-recognised awarding body.

A TLM representative said organisations increasingly needed to view respectful workplace practices as fundamental to business sustainability rather than simply an HR policy.

“A respectful workplace is not merely an optional perk or a policy on a piece of paper. It is the fundamental bedrock of sustainable business, human wellbeing and long-term organisational success,” the representative said.

The initiative would also give organisations a mechanism to continuously assess and improve their practices.

“This program is far more than just certification. It is a formal recognition of an organisation’s deep commitment to building a culture of respect, inclusion, accountability and professional excellence,” the representative added.

Applications close on September 30 2026 via www.wimglobalevents.com, with certification limited to 15 organisations annually.

The December program will also bring an international dimension through UK-based Sri Lankan professionals Deena Tissera and Lushani Kodituwakku, alongside local business and leadership figures chairing the three initiatives.

The WIM Leadership Awards Night will additionally recognise three business leaders for their wider contribution to Sri Lanka’s economy, industries and society.

Segera said the three platforms ultimately seek to take Sri Lankan business achievement beyond domestic recognition and position the country’s talent, entrepreneurs and corporate practices against international benchmarks.

“The world is no longer competing on quantity alone; it is competing on value, innovation, quality, talent and the ability to think beyond borders,” she said.

“Sri Lanka must prepare to compete, lead and make its mark — we simply cannot afford to be left behind.”

title: ITFC signs $ 1.5 b framework agreement with Maldives Govt. | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 18 September 2026 00:05
-     - 70

ITFC Chief Executive Officer Eng. Adeeb Yousuf Al-Aama (left) with Maldives Finance and Public Enterprises Minister and IsDB Governor for the Maldives Hassan Zareer

The International Islamic Trade Finance Corporation (ITFC), a member of the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB) Group, and the Government of the Republic of Maldives have signed a new five-year Framework Agreement. 

Under the agreement, ITFC will mobilise up to $ 1.5 billion to support trade financing operations in the Maldives between 2026 and 2031.

The agreement was signed at the Ministry of Finance and Public Enterprises in Malé recently by ITFC Chief Executive Officer Eng. Adeeb Yousuf Al-Aama and Maldives Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises and IsDB Governor for the Maldives Hassan Zareer during the ITFC CEO’s official visit to the country.

As part of the visit, Maldives President Dr. Mohamed Muizzu granted audience to CEO Eng. Adeeb Al-Aama, to discuss strengthening cooperation between ITFC and the Maldives and supporting the country’s economic priorities.

The Framework Agreement covers financing for the import of essential and strategic commodities, primarily through state owned enterprises, as well as lines of financing to local banks in the Maldives to support SMEs and the private sector. The parties will also explore trade-related technical assistance and advisory services to enhance trade capacity and market access, in line with the Maldives’ development agenda.

Minister Hassan Zareer said: “Since its establishment, ITFC has been a steadfast development partner to our nation. What began as crucial support for our energy requirements has evolved into a comprehensive partnership spanning the importation of staple foods and medical supplies, while catalysing growth in the vital sectors such as fisheries and SMEs. A key anchor of this relationship is the ongoing revolving trade finance facility extended to STO since 2017, which continues to provide vital liquidity support, ensuring uninterrupted bulk procurement of essential commodities and guaranteeing operational predictability for state trade. During periods of global volatility, ITFC has consistently proven to be among our most dependable development partners.”

ITFC CEO Al-Aama said: “This new Framework Agreement builds on a partnership that has developed over many years. Through the agreement, ITFC will work with the Government and its partners to mobilise financing for essential commodities as well as support to the private sector through local financial institutions. We will continue to work with the Maldives on the trade financing priorities identified by the Government whilst exploring further cooperation in the areas of trade development.”

The new agreement follows the first five-year Framework Agreement between ITFC and the Maldives, signed in 2019 and concluded in 2024, during which ITFC approved $ 1.7 billion.

Since its inception in 2008, ITFC has approved more than 

$ 3.3 billion in financing for the Maldives for the import of petroleum products, staple food, medicine and medical equipment, and construction materials, alongside financing for the private sector.

In addition to the signing, Eng. Adeeb Al-Aama held discussions with Maldives Minister of Finance and Public Enterprises Hassan Zareer and the Maldives Monetary Authority Governor Ahmed Munawar, on strengthening cooperation and exploring ways for further supporting the country’s economic priorities. He also met with STO Managing Director and CEO Shimad Ibrahim, and other senior officials of the Government.

title: Cabinet green lights  39 hospital infrastructure projects for 2027 rollout | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 18 September 2026 00:04
-     - 81

The Cabinet of Ministers has approved the implementation of 39 new development projects aimed at upgrading infrastructure across Government health service institutions, including hospitals, as part of a broader push to address long-standing infrastructure gaps and modernise health service facilities.

Cabinet Spokesman and Health Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa said earlier this week the projects stem from a review of 41 proposals submitted during 2025 and 2026, evaluated by the Department of National Planning. Following that evaluation, the Department recommended the projects be initiated from 2027, and they have since been incorporated into the Public Investment Program for 2027–2031.

“Of the 41 proposals reviewed, 39 were assessed as ready for implementation, with provisions for these to be allocated through the 2027 Budget,” Dr. Jayatissa said at the weekly post-Cabinet media briefing.

He said the 41 proposals focus on infrastructure development at tertiary-level institutions, including district, teaching, national and specialised hospitals.

Arogya centres modelled on global primary care push

Turning to the Government’s ‘Arogya’ wellness centre initiative, Dr. Jayatissa framed it as part of a decades-old global consensus on strengthening primary healthcare, tracing the approach back nearly five decades to the WHO’s Alma-Ata Declaration. 

Citing India’s Ayushman Bharat wellness centres as a reference model, he said Sri Lanka’s Arogyaya centres are intended to extend coverage to hospitals that were left out even under the World Bank-funded healthcare project of 2018–2019, while also covering provincial hospitals and B- and C-level facilities.

“Tertiary-level hospitals have reached capacity, particularly in OPD and clinic services, with patients often travelling long distances for care that could be delivered closer to home. The aim is to establish primary care facilities within a 1–2 kilometre radius, each designed to serve a defined population of around 10,000 patients,” he explained.

Leveraging advances in ICT, Dr. Jayatissa said the Government hopes to issue individuals a health number linked to their National Identity Card (NIC) number, enabling the maintenance of electronic health (e-health) records and allowing patients to be directed from primary care facilities to secondary, tertiary or specialised hospitals as needed.

Stating that the 2026 Budget allocated Rs. 1,500 million for this initiative, he said he hoped the Government would increase that allocation in the upcoming Budget 2027.

“Through this system, the Government intends to gradually reduce the patient population served per primary care centre from 10,000 to 5,000,” he added.

On staffing, Dr. Jayatissa said 260 Public Health Nursing Officers (PHNOs) have already been trained, with another 300 currently undergoing training. “We also plan to recruit an additional 500 PHNOs to support the rollout of primary healthcare service centres,” he added.

The Cabinet of Ministers has granted consent for the SAARC Energy Centre to conduct a training workshop themed ‘Financial Modelling for Renewable Energy Projects’ in Colombo from 5 to 7 October 2026, with Sri Lanka to extend hospitality for the event.

The workshop is expected to draw participation from two representatives of each SAARC member country, including Sri Lanka. The SAARC Energy Centre will provide all local hospitality facilities and airport transport for participants, excluding airfare.

Addressing the weekly post-Cabinet meeting media briefing, Cabinet Spokesman and Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa said the decision followed a proposal highlighting the workshop’s importance for building the capacity of public officers and other related parties in project evaluation and financial modelling within the renewable energy sector.

The proposal to this effect was submitted by Energy Minister Anura Karunathilake.

title: Ex-Navy Chief Karannagoda, Yoshitha Rajapaksa case fixed for pre-trial conference | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 18 September 2026 00:04
-     - 40

Former Navy Commander Admiral of the Fleet Wasantha Karannagoda

Yoshitha Rajapaksa

The Colombo High Court has ordered that the corruption case filed by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) against former Navy Commander Admiral of the Fleet Wasantha Karannagoda and Yoshitha Rajapaksa be called for a pre-trial conference on 13 October.

The case was taken up before Colombo High Court Judge Ravindra Premaratne yesterday, with both accused, who are out on bail, appearing before the court.

Appearing for Karannagoda, President’s Counsel Shavindra Fernando told the court that complete copies of certain statements submitted as evidence in the case had not been provided to the defence. President’s Counsel Sampath Mendis, appearing for Yoshitha Rajapaksa, separately requested clear copies of certain documents submitted by the CIABOC, saying some were unclear.

Responding, CIABOC Deputy Director General Ruwini Wickramasinghe said some of the documents sought by the defence had already been submitted to the High Court and could not be provided by the Commission, while those still in the CIABOC’s possession could be handed over.

After considering the submissions, the court ordered that the documents requested by the defence and currently in the court’s custody be provided, subject to payment of the prescribed fees. It also ordered that any other relevant documents held by the CIABOC be released to the defence.

The CIABOC has indicted the two accused on charges of committing a corruption offence by recruiting former President Mahinda Rajapaksa’s son, Yoshitha Rajapaksa, as a Cadet Officer to the executive branch of the Sri Lanka Navy in 2006 despite him not possessing the required qualifications, and by spending public funds to send him for training at the Royal Naval College in the United Kingdom outside established procedure.

title: Senior SLPP member remanded over permit corruption charges | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 18 September 2026 00:02
-     - 17

The Colombo Magistrate’s Court yesterday ordered that National Transport Commission Former Chairman Renuka Perera be remanded until 29 September, 2026, following his arrest by the Bribery Commission in connection with a corruption allegation.

The remand order was issued by Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama after considering submissions from Bribery Commission officials and Perera’s lawyers. Perera, a senior Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) figure, was produced before the court earlier in the day, after which the order was delivered.

Investigating officers told the court that Perera was arrested over the issuance of 56 passenger transport permits for the Southern Expressway in violation of regulations, and that he was taken into custody on charges of corruption.

According to the submissions, the permits were issued outside Cabinet approval, with 30 allocated to Perera’s committee and 26 distributed at his own discretion to individuals of his choice.

The Bribery Commission said it is conducting further investigations into the case.

title: PM, new Chinese envoy discuss education, digital transformation push | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 18 September 2026 00:00
-     - 23

Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya met with newly appointed Chinese Ambassador to Sri Lanka Wei Huaxiang at Temple Trees on  Wednesday, with discussions centred on deepening bilateral cooperation in education and digital transformation ahead of the 70th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries in 2027.

Ambassador Wei presented his credentials as Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary on 25 August, 2026.

A key focus of the talks was the Chinese Government’s continued support for providing school uniforms to Sri Lankan students. Both sides discussed shifting from the current annual arrangement to a longer-term framework spanning three to five years, aimed at ensuring the timely and predictable delivery of uniforms ahead of each new school year.

The two sides also reviewed progress on the Chinese-assisted digital education initiative, under which 900 smart devices are expected to support 500 smart classrooms across the country as part of Sri Lanka’s wider effort to digitalise its education sector.

Dr. Amarasuriya briefed Ambassador Wei on the Task Force on the Digital Transformation of Education, which is developing policy for digital education. Ambassador Wei welcomed the initiative and pledged China’s support for the Task Force’s work, with further engagement between the Task Force and the Chinese Embassy expected to follow.

Discussions further covered scholarship opportunities for Sri Lankan students under the Chinese Government Scholarship Program and the Chinese Ambassador’s Scholarship Program, along with the need for stronger regional and international cooperation on children’s online safety.

Dr. Amarasuriya thanked China for its assistance to Sri Lanka following Cyclone Ditwah and conveyed condolences over the loss and damage caused by recent landslides and floods in Tibetan border areas. The two sides also discussed cooperation on strengthening climate resilience.

title: Sri Lanka’s 156-strong Asian Games challenge: Beyond Rumesh, a wider medal hunt in Nagoya | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 18 September 2026 00:25
-     - 18

Sri Lankan contingent - 20th Asian Games

Rumesh Tharanga with The Ultimate Trophy

By Hishan Welmilla

Sri Lanka will send a 156-athlete contingent to the 20th Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, with 100 men and 56 women set to compete across 25 sports. The size of the team provides Sri Lanka with an opportunity to look beyond the traditional medal-winning disciplines and discover new heroes on one of Asia’s biggest sporting stages.

Team Sri Lanka will travel to Japan with a contingent of 156 athletes, comprising 100 male and 56 female athletes, who will compete across 25 sports disciplines.

The Sri Lankan contingent will compete across Aquatics – Swimming and Diving, Archery, Artistic Gymnastics, Judo, Rowing, Rugby Sevens, Table Tennis, Squash, Weightlifting, Wrestling, Basketball 3x3, Wushu, Kabaddi, Beach Volleyball, Athletics, Boxing, Karate, Sailing, Taekwondo, Surfing, Badminton, Cricket, Golf, Modern Pentathlon and Hockey.

The Asian Games begin on 19 September and run until 4 October, bringing together the continent’s strongest sporting nations. For Sri Lanka, the challenge will be considerable, but there are several areas where the contingent can realistically aspire to make an impact.

Athletics carries the biggest individual hopes

Athletics remains central to Sri Lanka’s Asian Games ambitions. Historically, it has been the country’s most successful sport at the Games, producing 11 of Sri Lanka’s 12 Asian Games gold medals. Cricket has supplied the other gold. Sri Lanka has won 51 medals overall at the Asian Games.

The spotlight, naturally, will fall on Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage.

The 23-year-old javelin thrower has emerged as one of the most prominent athletes in world athletics. His recent performances include throws of 92.62 metres in Rome and 92.07m in Zurich, while he also captured the Diamond League Final with 89.04m. World Athletics lists him as Sri Lanka’s leading javelin athlete.

His Asian Games campaign, however, has been complicated by an unusual setback. Three of his key competition javelins were reportedly damaged during air transportation. Those implements were associated with his 92.62m, 92.07m and 91.09m performances.

The equipment problem will therefore be an additional challenge, but Tharanga enters Nagoya with a formidable competitive record and considerable international experience.

Cricket remains a major medal opportunity

Cricket will again be one of Sri Lanka’s major medal avenues. The sport has already produced an Asian Games gold for the country, and the return of T20 cricket gives Sri Lanka an opportunity to use its depth and experience in the shortest format.

The cricket competition also has wider significance for Japan. The country is using the Asian Games to promote the sport, with Sri Lanka among the major cricket nations participating in the tournament.

Rugby Sevens can produce a surprise

Sri Lanka’s rugby Sevens teams have traditionally possessed the speed and attacking ability to trouble stronger Asian opponents. In a short tournament, the format can produce unexpected results, particularly when a team is able to maintain discipline and fitness across successive matches.

A strong start could put Sri Lanka into contention for the latter stages, although the Asian competition remains extremely demanding.

Rowing, badminton and squash

Rowing is another discipline where Sri Lanka will look for individual performances to translate into finals and potential podium opportunities. The sport demands exceptional preparation, and even a place among the leading crews would represent an important benchmark.

In badminton, Sri Lanka’s challenge will be particularly demanding given the strength of countries such as China, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, India and Chinese Taipei. Nevertheless, the exposure gained by Sri Lankan players against this level of opposition could be valuable for the next generation.

Squash is another sport capable of producing competitive performances. Sri Lanka has a history of producing technically accomplished players, and the Asian Games provide an opportunity to measure that talent against some of the world’s strongest squash nations.

Combat sports and strength disciplines

Sri Lanka’s prospects should not be confined to the headline sports.

Boxing, judo, karate, wushu, wrestling and weightlifting all provide opportunities for athletes to progress through the draw and challenge established Asian competitors.

Combat sports can be particularly unpredictable. A single outstanding performance can change an athlete’s tournament, making these disciplines important to watch even when Sri Lanka enters without the same international profile as the continent’s leading nations.

Sailing also deserves attention. Sri Lanka has previously won an Asian Games silver medal in the sport, demonstrating that the country has the ability to compete at continental level.

The bigger picture

The significance of Nagoya should therefore extend beyond the final medal tally.

Sri Lanka is taking a sizeable group of athletes across 25 disciplines, giving many competitors the opportunity to experience a level of competition that cannot be replicated domestically.

For some, the target will be a medal. For others, reaching a final, establishing a personal best or defeating a higher-ranked opponent could become the foundation for future international success.

And above them all stands Rumesh Tharanga.

If the javelin star can reproduce anything close to his extraordinary 2026 form, his performance could become one of the defining stories of Sri Lanka’s Nagoya campaign. But Sri Lanka’s Asian Games challenge should not be reduced to one athlete.

The 156-member team represents 25 different sporting journeys — and Nagoya could reveal that Sri Lanka’s next generation of Asian Games heroes extends well beyond the javelin runway.

title: Dinusha honoured by ICC with Player of the Month award | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 18 September 2026 00:06
-     - 7

ICC Men's Player of the Month Sonal Dinusha

Sri Lanka batter Sonal Dinusha has been named the ICC Player of the Month for August following his gritty knocks against India in a home ICC World Test Championship series, while Isle of Man Captain Lucy Barnett has won the women’s award for her standout performances in the Continental Cup T20I tournament.

Dinusha, who won the award in a competitive group that included fast bowlers Ollie Robinson of England and Hasan Mahmud of Bangladesh, struck three centuries in four innings in the two-Test series against India, which included twin centuries in a fighting draw in the latter match.

The 25-year-old left-hander had scores of 100 and 84 in the first Test in Galle that his team lost, but his knocks of 103 and 133 not out in the second one at the Sinhalese Sports Club ground in Colombo helped stave off defeat from a difficult situation.

In saving the match, he became only the third batter ever to score a century in each innings for a team that was asked to follow on. The award was credible not only because it came in the face of some stiff competition from Robinson and Hasan but also because Dinusha got it after only five international matches - all Tests.

Sonal Dinusha said: “This recognition means so much to me, especially so early in my career, and I’m truly grateful to the ICC for this honour. The series against India will always hold a special place in my heart. Scoring three centuries was a dream come true, made even more meaningful by achieving them in Colombo and Galle in front of our home fans.”

“Although we didn’t get the overall result we hoped for, the way our team fought back in the second match showed the character, belief and determination we have as a side. I’m proud to have shared that fight with my teammates.”

“Representing Sri Lanka is a privilege I never take for granted, and this recognition gives me even more motivation to keep learning, improving and contributing to the team. I’ll continue to give my very best for Sri Lanka in the months and years ahead.”

“I’m deeply thankful to my parents, teammates, coaches, friends and relatives for their constant love, support and belief in me. This achievement is not mine alone; it belongs to everyone who has been part of my journey and helped me reach this point.”

By Shamseer Jaleel

Sri Lankan schools rugby will enter a new chapter with the launch of the inaugural NEXT XV franchise rugby tournament, bringing together 140 schoolboy players in a four-team competition from 19 September to 10 October at CR and FC Ground, Longdon Place.

The first game will kick off tomorrow (19) at 6 pm, and the second game will be at 8 p.m.

The tournament will feature four franchises: Colombo Aces, Kandy Tuskers, Galle Lions and Jaffna Bulls, with each squad comprising 35 players. Organisers have also guaranteed game time for every player during the four-week competition, making it one of the biggest talent development initiatives introduced in schools rugby.

NEXT XV will serve as the official national selection tournament for Sri Lanka Rugby. National selectors will closely monitor performances before naming a 40-member training squad for the Junior Asia Rugby Tournament, which Sri Lanka will host in Colombo this December.

The regional championship will feature Sri Lanka, Hong Kong China, Chinese Taipei and South Korea, with the winners securing Asia’s qualification berth for the 2027 Junior World Rugby Tournament.

The competition will begin with a three-round league stage before culminating in the third-place playoff and the grand final on 10 October.

Several leading school captains and standout performers from the recently concluded Schools Elite Rugby Sevens Championship have been drafted into the franchises. title: Champions Tamil Union pick up Rs. 2 m, dominate awards | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 18 September 2026 00:02
-     - 10

Tamil Union led by former Sri Lanka wicket-keeper/batsman Minod Bhanuka collected a prize money of Rs. 2 million as champions of the Major Club T20 tournament and also dominated the individual awards.

In the final played under lights at the R Premadasa Cricket Stadium on Wednesday, Tamil Union beat SSC by seven wickets to clinch their first Major Club T20 title.

What was most inspiring is that Tamil Union went through the entire tournament unbeaten in the nine matches they played – 6 in the group stage and three in the knockout.

They dominated the individual awards with Sineth Jayawardena picking up the Player of the Final award of Rs. 500,000 for his brilliant knock of 82 off 32 balls, Vijayakanth Viyaskanth the Best Bowler’s award of Rs. 750,000 for his 17 wickets (avg. 13.05) making him the leading wicket-taker in the tournament and Navod Paranavithana the Most Valuable Player award of 

Rs. 1 million.

The only individual award that evaded Tamil Union was for the Best Batsman (Rs. 750,000) that was won by Sohan de Livera of Moors SC. SSC as runner-up picked up prize money of Rs. 1.5 million.

The awards were presented by Prasanna Fernando, chairman of Domestic Cricket Committee and Chinthaka Edirimanne, head of National Cricket Operations, SLC. (ST)
